title: Why RED Is Literally Everywhere During Chinese New Year
description: Red envelopes, red lanterns, red everything. But why red specifically? The origin story is wilder than you think. What color means luck in YOUR culture?

sections.narration: Imagine walking through Chinatown in January and literally everything is bright red.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy walking under red lanterns, red banners, warm street

sections.narration: Red lanterns, red envelopes, red clothes — even the underwear is red, seriously.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy surrounded by red items floating around him, warm scene

sections.narration: Your friend's grandma hands you a red envelope and says it'll bring you luck.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy receiving red envelope from elderly woman, golden warm light

sections.narration: So the story goes that a legendary creature called Nian used to terrorize villages.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy reading storybook, friendly dragon illustration, warm tones

sections.narration: People discovered that Nian was scared of three things — loud noise, fire, and red.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy holding firecracker, lantern, red banner, warm village scene

sections.narration: And it gets weirder — they basically decorated the entire village red to keep it away.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy painting door red, red decorations everywhere, warm sunset

sections.narration: But here's the thing — red also symbolizes joy, prosperity, and good fortune in Chinese culture.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy next to Chinese character for fortune in red, golden glow

sections.narration: It's not just for New Year — red shows up at weddings, birthdays, and celebrations too.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy at festive table with red decorations, warm celebration scene

sections.narration: So THAT'S why red envelopes have money inside — you're wrapping luck in protection.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy opening red envelope with golden coins, warm sparkle effect

sections.narration: Every red decoration is basically a centuries-old shield against bad vibes.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy beneath red archway, peaceful village behind, warm sunset

sections.narration: Next Chinese New Year, you'll see all that red and know the real story behind it.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy smiling under red lanterns, festive warm night scene
